title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Departure Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Departure Board
options.lineage: Mumbai suburban railway: split-flap boards, enamel platform signage, working timetables
options.thesis: The portfolio as a station information system: routing, scheduling, and throughput, the same engineering Tanuv ships.
options.viewport: A departure board spans the first viewport: Tanuv Nair as the station name, role and availability as the next departure, flaps settling into place.
options.risk: Theme-park nostalgia if the flaps animate without carrying real information.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.thesis: Quantities as the interface: the person measured in glowing tube banks.
options.case: Strong audience pull, but the grammar is numeric display and the honest facts here are not mostly numbers; clarity strains.

options.label: One-Bit Desktop
options.thesis: The site as a dithered desktop: windows for sections, pixel icons for proof.
options.case: Beloved by engineers, but window management inserts a layer between a ten-second scan and the facts.

options.label: Thirty-Two Folds
options.lineage: origami instruction diagrams, one uncut sheet
options.thesis: The career as a crane sequence: each project a deliberate fold carrying every earlier crease.
options.case: Beautiful discipline, but a sequential fold hides the whole bird from a recruiter's glance.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The clean engineer portfolio: hero, project cards, skills row, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A light sans-serif hero with name, role, a project card grid, and a trimmed skills row.
